title: Chang'e and the Jade Rabbit
credit: From the old Chinese story of Chang'e, the lady in the moon, and Hou Yi the archer, told at the Mid-Autumn Festival for more than two thousand years and written down in English by Richard Wilhelm (1921) and E. T. C. Werner (1922). Retold in our own words.
status: Locked at STOP 1 (Eddie, 2026-11-17: "A on all three"), then PROVISIONAL storytelling-pull edits (BOOK-STANDARD "Storytelling pull", P1-P18) for Eddie's morning read: the changed lines and why are in renders/review/chang-e-stop1/STORY-PULL.md; the locked text is commit 71556cc4f.

lines.text: Long ago in China, there were ten suns. They were ten little sun-birds, and they lived in a great tree by the Eastern Sea.
say: Long ago in China, there were ten suns. They were ten little sun-birds, and they lived in a great tree by the Eastern Sea.

lines.text: Every morning, one sun-bird flew across the sky. The other nine waited for their turn.
say: Every morning, one sun-bird flew across the sky. The other nine waited for their turn.

lines.text: But one morning, the ten suns said, "Let's all fly together! It will be fun!"
say: But one morning, the ten suns said,
Let's all fly together! It will be fun!

lines.text: Zoom! Up they flew, all ten at once. Ten suns in one sky!
say: Zoom! Up they flew, all ten at once. Ten suns in one sky!

lines.text: Far below, the whole earth grew hot, hot, hot.
say: Far below, the whole earth grew hot, hot,... hot.

lines.text: The rivers dried up. The rice turned brown. Even the frogs hid in the mud.
say: The rivers dried up. The rice turned brown. Even the frogs hid in the... mud.

lines.text: In a little village lived Hou Yi, the best archer in all the land, and his kind wife, Chang'e.
say: In a little village lived Hoe Yee, the best archer in all the land, and his kind wife, Chahng-uh.

lines.text: Chang'e gave cool water to everyone: to the children, to the old people, and to a little white rabbit with hot, sore feet.
say: Chahng-uh gave cool water to everyone: to the children, to the old people, and to a little white rabbit with hot, sore feet.

lines.text: Hou Yi called up to the sky. "Suns! Please take turns! The earth is too hot!"
say: Hoe Yee called up to the sky.
Suns! Please take turns! The earth is too hot!

lines.text: But the ten suns were having too much fun to listen.
say: But the ten suns were having too much fun to listen.

lines.text: So Hou Yi and Chang'e walked all the way to the Eastern Sea. Hou Yi took his red bow and ten arrows.
say: So Hoe Yee and Chahng-uh walked all the way to the Eastern Sea. Hoe Yee took his red bow and ten arrows.

lines.text: Whoosh! His arrow hit a sun, and its fire went out. A little gold bird tumbled into the cool sea. Splash!
say: Whoosh! His arrow hit a sun, and its fire went out. A little gold bird tumbled into the cool sea. Splash!

lines.text: Whoosh! Whoosh! One by one, nine suns fell into the sea. They were not hurt. They were only cool and wet.
say: Whoosh! Whoosh! One by one, nine suns fell into the... sea. They were not hurt. They were only cool and wet.

lines.text: "Stop!" called Chang'e. "Leave one sun, to keep the world warm." So Hou Yi put away his last arrow.
say: Leave one sun, to keep the world warm.
So Hoe Yee put away his last arrow.

lines.text: The nine wet sun-birds flew home to their tree, and the suns took turns again. Then something fell from the sky. Pitter-patter!
say: The nine wet sun-birds flew home to their tree, and the suns took turns again. Then something fell from the sky. Pitter-patter!

lines.text: It was rain! The rice grew green, and everyone cheered for Hou Yi. Boom, boom went the drums!
say: It was rain! The rice grew green, and everyone cheered for Hoe Yee. Boom, boom went the drums!

lines.text: Then the Queen Mother of the West came down on a cloud. "You saved the earth," she said. "Here is a gift."
say: Then the Queen Mother of the West came down on a cloud.

lines.text: She gave Hou Yi a little jade bottle. "This is magic medicine. The one who drinks it will float up to the sky and live forever. But there is only enough for one."
say: She gave Hoe Yee a little jade bottle.
This is magic medicine. The one who drinks it will float up to the sky and live forever. But there is only enough for... one.

lines.text: "I don't want to live forever without Chang'e," said Hou Yi. "And I would never go without you," said Chang'e.
say: I don't want to live forever without Chahng-uh,
And I would never go without you,

lines.text: So they put the little bottle high on a shelf, and they stayed together on the earth, with the little white rabbit. But someone was watching from behind the osmanthus tree.
say: So they put the little bottle high on a shelf, and they stayed together on the earth, with the little white rabbit. But someone was watching from behind the osmanthus tree.

lines.text: It was Feng Meng, Hou Yi's student. Feng Meng was good with a bow, but he had a greedy heart.
say: It was Fung Mung, Hoe Yee's student. Fung Mung was good with a bow, but he had a greedy heart.

lines.text: One night, when Hou Yi was away, Feng Meng crept up to the house. "Give me the magic medicine!" he said. "I want to live forever!"
say: One night, when Hoe Yee was away, Fung Mung crept up to the house.

lines.text: Chang'e took the little bottle from the shelf and held it tight. "No," she said. "Magic is not for a greedy heart."
say: Chahng-uh took the little bottle from the shelf and held it tight.
Magic is not for a greedy heart.

lines.text: Feng Meng reached out to grab it. So, quick as a wink, Chang'e drank the medicine herself. Gulp!
say: Fung Mung reached out to grab it. So, quick as a wink, Chahng-uh drank the medicine herself. Gulp!

lines.text: At once she felt as light as a feather. Her feet left the floor, and she began to float!
say: At once she felt as light as a... feather. Her feet left the floor, and she began to float!

lines.text: Up, up she floated, over the roof and the osmanthus tree. Feng Meng slipped and sat down, bump! Then he ran away with empty hands.
say: Up, up she floated, over the roof and the osmanthus tree. Fung Mung slipped and sat down, bump! Then he ran away with empty hands.

lines.text: Just then, Hou Yi came running home, pat-pat-pat! "Chang'e!" he called. But she was too high to reach.
say: Just then, Hoe Yee came running home, pat-pat-pat!
he called. But she was too high to reach.

lines.text: "Hou Yi!" called Chang'e. "I will stay where you can see me!" But the magic carried her higher and higher, past the clouds.
say: I will stay where you can see me!
But the magic carried her higher and higher, past the clouds.

lines.text: The stars were far, far away. So Chang'e stopped at the moon, the place in the sky closest to home.
say: The stars were far, far away. So Chahng-uh stopped at the... moon, the place in the sky closest to home.

lines.text: Hou Yi looked up at the moon, bright and round, all night long. Up there, was Chang'e all alone?
say: Hoe Yee looked up at the moon, bright and round, all night long. Up there, was Chahng-uh all alone?

lines.text: The moon was silver and cold and very, very quiet. There was a jade palace, an osmanthus tree, and nobody else.
say: The moon was silver and cold and very, very quiet. There was a jade palace, an osmanthus tree, and nobody else.

lines.text: "Am I all alone up here?" said Chang'e softly, and a tear rolled down her cheek.
say: Am I all alone up here?
said Chahng-uh softly, and a tear rolled down her cheek.

lines.text: Then something wriggled in her ribbon. Out popped the little white rabbit! He held on all the way up.
say: Then something wriggled in her ribbon. Out popped the little white rabbit! He held on all the way up.

lines.text: "You were my friend on the earth," said the rabbit. "So I will be your friend on the moon." He filled a jade bowl with golden osmanthus flowers.
say: You were my friend on the earth,
So I will be your friend on the moon.
He filled a jade bowl with golden osmanthus flowers.

lines.text: Thump, thump, thump! The rabbit pounded the flowers. "What are you making?" asked Chang'e. "You will see!" said the rabbit. And far below, someone was looking up.
say: Thump, thump,... thump! The rabbit pounded the flowers.
said the rabbit. And far below, someone was looking up.

lines.text: It was Hou Yi. Down on the earth, he missed Chang'e every day.
say: It was Hoe Yee. Down on the earth, he missed Chahng-uh every day.

lines.text: On the night of the full moon, he put her favourite things in the garden: round cakes, sweet fruit and a cup of tea.
say: On the night of the full moon, he put her favourite things in the garden: round cakes, sweet fruit and a cup of tea.

lines.text: Tip-tap, tip-tap! The village children came running with lanterns: rabbit lanterns, fish lanterns and lotus lanterns.
say: Tip-tap, tip-tap! The village children came running with lanterns: rabbit lanterns, fish lanterns and lotus lanterns.

lines.text: "Look up at the moon!" said Hou Yi. "Let's make the brightest lights, so Chang'e can see us!"
say: Let's make the brightest lights, so Chahng-uh can see us!

lines.text: One by one, the lanterns glowed, like little moons all over the garden. Would Chang'e see them?
say: One by one, the lanterns glowed, like little... moons all over the garden. Would Chahng-uh see them?

lines.text: Up on the moon, Chang'e looked down. Far below, tiny lights were twinkling in a garden.
say: Up on the moon, Chahng-uh looked down. Far below, tiny lights were twinkling in a garden.

lines.text: "Lanterns!" said Chang'e. "Hou Yi has lit lanterns for me! But how can he see me?"
say: Hoe Yee has lit lanterns for me! But how can he see me?

lines.text: "Now I can show you," said the rabbit. He tipped his jade bowl, and out poured silver moonlight!
say: said the rabbit. He tipped his jade bowl, and out poured silver moonlight!

lines.text: Whoosh! Together they threw the moonlight up high, and the moon shone round and bright, brighter than ever before.
say: Whoosh! Together they threw the moonlight up high, and the moon shone round and... bright, brighter than ever before.

lines.text: Far below, Hou Yi saw Chang'e and the little rabbit in the shining moon. He waved, and Chang'e waved back. Could they do it again?
say: Far below, Hoe Yee saw Chahng-uh and the little rabbit in the shining moon. He waved, and Chahng-uh waved back. Could they do it again?

lines.text: Yes! Every year, on the night of the full moon in autumn, Hou Yi lit lanterns, and Chang'e and the rabbit made the moon shine its brightest.
say: Yes! Every year, on the night of the full moon in autumn, Hoe Yee lit lanterns, and Chahng-uh and the rabbit made the moon shine its brightest.

lines.text: Soon all the families came out to look at the moon, and they lit lanterns too.
say: Soon all the families came out to look at the moon, and they lit lanterns too.

lines.text: They shared round mooncakes, because a round moon and a round cake mean the whole family is together.
say: They shared round mooncakes, because a round moon and a round cake mean the whole family is together.

lines.text: Boom-ba-boom! This is the Mid-Autumn Festival, the night of the brightest moon.
say: Boom-ba-boom! This is the Mid-Autumn Festival, the night of the brightest moon.

lines.text: Look up at the moon! Can you see the rabbit? Wave to Chang'e! Someone you love is looking at the same moon.
say: Look up at the... moon! Can you see the rabbit? Wave to Chahng-uh! Someone you love is looking at the same moon.

moral.text: Chang'e was up on the moon, and Hou Yi was down on the earth. They were far apart.
say: Chahng-uh was up on the moon, and Hoe Yee was down on the earth. They were far apart.

moral.text: But they still shared the same moon. He lit lanterns for her, and she made the moon shine for him.
say: But they still shared the same moon. He lit lanterns for her, and she made the moon shine for him.

moral.text: When you miss someone, look up at the moon. The people you love can see it too.
say: When you miss someone, look up at the moon. The people you love can see it too.

moral.text: Far or near, love shines like the moon.
say: Far or near, love shines like the... moon.

game.text: The suns want to play! Tap each sun to wake it up, and count them.
say: The suns want to play! Tap each sun to wake it up, and count them.

game.text: Ten suns, ready to fly!
Help Chang'e! Tap everyone who needs water.
say: Help Chahng-uh! Tap everyone who needs water.

game.text: Cool water for everyone. Ahh!
Help Hou Yi cool the suns! Tap the suns, one by one.
say: Help Hoe Yee cool the suns! Tap the suns, one by one.

game.text: Splash, splash! The suns are cool and wet.
say: Splash, splash! The suns are cool and wet.

game.text: Everyone is cheering! The drums play a song. Can you play it back?
say: Everyone is cheering! The drums play a song. Can you play it back?

game.text: Boom, boom, clang! What a happy song!
say: Boom, boom, clang! What a happy song!

game.text: Someone came to the window! Move the lantern to see his shadow.
say: Someone came to the window! Move the lantern to see his shadow.

game.text: It is Feng Meng! What does he want?
say: It is Fung Mung! What does he want?

game.text: Look closely! Who is holding on to Chang'e's ribbon? Tap him!
say: Look closely! Who is holding on to Chahng-uh's ribbon? Tap him!

game.text: The little white rabbit! Shh, Chang'e does not know yet.
say: The little white rabbit! Shh, Chahng-uh does not know yet.

game.text: Help the rabbit pound! Tap when the stick comes down. Thump!
say: Help the rabbit pound! Tap when the stick comes down. Thump!

game.text: Thump, thump, thump! Good pounding!
Light the lanterns! Tap each one.
say: Light the lanterns! Tap each one.

game.text: So many little moons! Can Chang'e see them?
say: So many little moons! Can Chahng-uh see them?

game.text: The bowl needs more! Tap the golden flowers to toss them in.
say: The bowl needs more! Tap the golden flowers to toss them in.

say: Full to the top! Now watch!

game.text: Share the mooncake! Give a piece to everyone.
say: Share the mooncake! Give a piece to everyone.

notes.twist: Old story: Hou Yi shoots nine suns dead; Chang'e takes the medicine (in some tellings to live forever herself, in others to keep it from a thief) and is left alone in a cold palace, sometimes turned into a toad, sorry for ever. Ours: no sun is hurt (nine fall into the sea, cool and wet, and the suns take turns again), and it is Chang'e who says "leave one"; she drinks the medicine bravely so a greedy heart cannot have it, and she keeps her promise to Hou Yi as best she can: "I will stay where you can see me!" (6.3), stopping at the moon, the place in the sky closest to home; she is not alone, because the little rabbit she gave water to held on to her ribbon all the way up (the reader spots him in spread 6 before she does); and the Jade Rabbit is not pounding forever-medicine but moonlight, so the Mid-Autumn moon shines bright enough to answer Hou Yi's lanterns (7.5 plants it, 9.3 pays it off). The reader cools the suns, lights the lanterns and fills the rabbit's bowl.
notes.moral: Far or near, love shines like the moon.
notes.changes: 1 the ten suns are sun-birds (the golden crows of Chinese art) and none is hurt. 2 the Queen Mother of the West gives the medicine (as in the Huainanzi tellings): the same Queen Mother as book 5. 3 Feng Meng is greedy and silly, never armed; he runs off with empty hands. 4 left out: Emperor Yao, any punishment, Chang'e as a toad, Wu Gang and his axe, Hou Yi's death. 5 the rabbit in the moon is real: the dark patches of the full moon, seen as a rabbit with a pounding stick across China, Korea and Japan. 6 the Mid-Autumn Festival is the 15th day of the 8th lunar month; lanterns and mooncakes as families keep it today.
